def factor_volume_spike_tail_corr(df):
    """Relative-volume return tail stress preserving negative correlation mechanism."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    is_high_vol, is_low_vol, vol_ratio = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(df_copy["volume"], window=20)
    vol_ratio = vol_ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    corr = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=20).corr(vol_ratio)
    downside = ret.clip(upper=0.0)
    downside_std = downside.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=1)
    stress = (-corr) * downside_std
    df_copy["factor_volume_spike_tail_corr"] = stress.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
    return df_copy["factor_volume_spike_tail_corr"]
description: Mutation of tail_stress_vol_ret_corr_0002. Preserves the core tail-risk mechanism: negative rolling correlation between returns and volume signals distribution/accumulation under stress, amplified by downside severity. The bottleneck in the parent was use of raw volume, whose cross-sectional scale confounds the correlation and weakens signal after industry/size neutralization. This child replaces raw volume with the continuous volume/EMA ratio from alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime, which is a relative-volume surprise measure, removing level effects while keeping the same dynamic dependence. One lightweight modifier: 5-day smoothing of the stress score to reduce noise. The signal remains raw and single-stock; cross-sectional normalization is left to the engine gate.
